newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa's Mandela plans to loaf in retirement.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela plans to loaf in retirement.

text.p: South Africa's President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday he planned a lazy retirement after quitting politics.
"I am asked what I am going to do when I retire. The answer is simple -- I am going to loaf," Mandela, 78, told businessmen during a visit to Zimbabwe.
"I will be without a job and I will have to stand by the roadside with a board which says: 'Unemployed, please help'," he joked.

Mandela, who was jailed for 27 years under apartheid and became president in South Africa's first all-race election three years ago, does not plan to stand for a second term in 1999. He is already preparing the way for a smooth handover to his likely successor, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki.
Mbeki is expected to be chosen as leader of the ruling African National Congress when Mandela steps down from the party post in December.
